newsitem.title: USA: Dreyfus offers hybrid investor account.
newsitem.headline: Dreyfus offers hybrid investor account.

text.p: Dreyfus Corp said it introduced a new asset management account that borrows elements from private banking and wrap accounts and lowers the threshold on asset requirements.
The hybrid service, Dreyfus Masterpiece, offers a customized asset management and trust service for individuals with assets of $200,000 to $1 million.

"Dreyfus Masterpiece was created to provide investors with the type of custom-tailored investment management and trust services once reserved only for the very wealthy," said Paul Kochis, director of the Masterpiece program.
The service is "clearly an attempt by Dreyfus to offer a wider range of service than is typically offered to the mutual fund purchaser," Kochis said in an interview.

Kochis said he would like the Masterpiece program to attract about $100 million in assets within the next three years and estimated the total target market at about $100 billion, which currently sit in wrap accounts.

Dreyfus will team with parent Mellon Bank Corp and Mellon unit Boston Co to offer customers a one-on-one relationship with a Dreyfus portfolio advisor as well as help on financial management, and access to tax and estate planning.
Under the service, investors also receive quarterly performance reports.
The service will initially be offered in New York, New Jersey and Connecticut.
Kochis said the program is aimed to fill "the middle end of the spectrum...our real focus is that broad middle market, the average American investor."
Kochis estimated that at least 2.5 million U.S. households have $200,000-$1 million in assets. The top 10 mutual fund companies have captured about 200,000 of those accounts.
